faq.q: このツールは何を測定しますか？
faq.a: 企業・品質・コンプライアンス・生産・サプライチェーン・ドキュメントの 6 つの領域で 0–100 のスコアを出します。高いほどリスクが高いことを示します。

faq.q: スコアは最終的な查核結果ですか？
faq.a: いいえ。スコアはお客様がお答えになった内容に基づく一次評価です。確定的な查核結果は、レポートをダウンロードの上、サプライヤー查核サービスをご検討ください。

faq.q: サプライヤーは私の回答内容を見ますか？
faq.a: いいえ。回答内容を保存するか第三者が見ることはありません。スコアはブラウザ内で完結します。

faq.q: サプライヤーの名前や住所が分からなくても使えますか？
faq.a: はい。スコアは一般的なリスク要因に基づくため、名前が分からなくても意味のある結果が得られます。

faq.q: もっと厳密な查核が必要と判断された場合は？
faq.a: レポート画面から正式なサプライヤー查核を申し込むか、工場監査を予約できます。

faq.q: What is a supplier verification checklist?
faq.a: A set of documents and checks you complete before ordering. It shows the company is a real legal entity, the factory exists and can make your product, and the quality, compliance and commercial terms are agreed in writing.

faq.q: Which checks matter most?
faq.a: The critical ones: business licence and registration cross-check, confirmed factory address, evidence the site is real such as photos or live video, confirmation of manufacturer versus trading company, product test reports, product compliance for your market, and a signed contract with agreed specifications.

faq.q: Does ticking every box mean the supplier is safe?
faq.a: No. This is a self-assessment built on what the supplier gives you, and documents can be forged. Only an independent verification or factory audit confirms the claims on the ground.

faq.q: Is my progress saved?
faq.a: Yes. Your ticks are stored in your browser, so you can close the page and come back. Use print or save as PDF to keep a copy for your supplier file.

page.lead: 20 GP、40 GP、40 HQ、または冷凍コンテナに何個のカートンが収まるか、そして出荷に必要なコンテナの数を計算します。
page.quickAnswer: カートンの寸法、単位重量、合計数量を入力します。電卓は、各容器の内部寸法に対して6つの箱の向きをすべてテストし、最も多くのカートンに合った配置を維持してから、ペイロード制限を適用します。コンテナごとの単位、必要なコンテナ、およびボリュームとペイロードの使用率を返します。
page.how1: All six carton orientations are tested against the container's internal length, width and height.
page.how2: The arrangement with the highest count wins, after subtracting the gap you set between cartons.
page.how3: The payload limit is applied: units per container cannot exceed max payload divided by unit weight.
page.how4: Containers needed is total quantity divided by units per container, rounded up.
page.specsLead: Typical ISO specifications. Actual figures vary by carrier, container owner and build year.
page.methodBody: The result is a theoretical maximum from a rectangular packing model. It assumes cartons are rigid, stackable and can be rotated, and that the load is evenly distributed. Real loading is affected by pallets, dunnage, carton deformation, stacking strength, axle weight rules and stowage order. Treat the output as a planning estimate and confirm the final plan with your forwarder or loading supervisor.
page.metaDesc: Free container loading calculator for 20GP, 40GP, 40HQ, 45HQ and reefer containers. Work out cartons per container, containers needed, volume and payload utilisation.

ui.clearanceHelp: Leave 2–5 cm for dunnage, strapping and carton bulge.
ui.allowRotateHelp: Tests all six orientations and keeps the best fit.
ui.warnOverweight: The load reaches the payload limit before the container is full. Weight, not space, is the binding constraint.
ui.warnTooLarge: These cartons are too large to fit any container in this list. Check the dimensions.
ui.warnDoor: The carton may not pass through the door opening in this orientation. Check with your loading team.

faq.q: What is the difference between a 40GP and a 40HQ?
faq.a: Both are the same length and width. A 40HQ is about 30 cm taller inside (269 cm versus 239 cm), which adds roughly 9 m³ of capacity. The payload limit is nearly identical, so the high cube only helps when you run out of space before you run out of weight.

faq.q: Why is your number different from my forwarder's?
faq.a: Three common reasons. First, container internal dimensions vary slightly by carrier and build year. Second, this model assumes cartons are rigid and fully stackable, while real loading needs pallets, dunnage and tolerances. Third, weight distribution and road axle limits can cap the load below the container's maximum payload.

faq.q: Should I set a gap between cartons?
faq.a: Yes, for planning. Set 2 to 5 cm if cartons are packed by hand or may bulge. Set 0 only for rigid, uniform cartons on a tightly controlled load.

faq.q: Does this handle pallets?
faq.a: Not directly in this version. To approximate a palletised load, enter the pallet footprint and height including the pallet base as one unit, and set the quantity to your pallet count.

faq.q: Are these container specifications exact?
faq.a: No. They are widely used typical figures for planning. Dimensions and payload limits differ by container owner, manufacturer and build year, and shipping lines publish their own limits. Confirm with your carrier before booking.

faq.q: What if my cartons cannot be stacked?
faq.a: Enter the carton height as the full stack height you are willing to allow, or reduce the quantity per layer manually. This version assumes every carton carries the load above it.

faq.q: ツールを使うのにお金はかかりますか？
faq.a: かかりません。リスク計算機、チェックリスト、スコアカードはすべて無料で、アカウント登録も不要です。料金が発生するのは、サプライヤーの核查や監査をご依頼いただいたときだけです。

faq.q: サプライヤー核查の費用はいくらですか？
faq.a: サプライヤーごとに見積もります。価格は国、現場訪問を含むかどうか、レビューが必要な書類の数によって変わります。会社名をお送りください。すぐに見積もりします。

faq.q: 工場監査の費用はいくらですか？
faq.a: 人日単位の料金に交通費を加算して見積もります。単一拠点の品質監査は 1 人日から、SMETA のような本格的な社会的責任監査は通常 2 人日以上（従業員数による）かかります。

faq.q: サプライヤーモニタリングはどのように機能しますか？
faq.a: モニタリングはサブスクリプションで、サプライヤーごとに年額で見積もります。ご指定の周期で確認済み事項を再確認し、変化があったときに短い更新をお送りします。まず単発の核查から始めて、後からモニタリングを追加することもできます。

methodology.h1: How Our Supplier Risk Assessment Works
methodology.lead: Risk scores are calculated by a deterministic rules engine with published weights. The same inputs always produce the same score. Language models are used only to explain a result in plain language, and they cannot change the number.
methodology.quickAnswer: We score a supplier across six weighted dimensions: company, quality, compliance, production, supply chain and documentation. Each answer you give maps to one dimension, contributes a weighted risk value, and rolls up into an overall figure out of 100, where higher means more risk. Missing evidence raises the score rather than being treated as neutral. The weights shown below are read directly from the scoring model, not typed by hand.
methodology.frameworkBody: Each question belongs to one dimension. Within a dimension, answers carry a risk value between 0 and 100. The dimension score is the weighted mean of its answered questions, and the overall score is the weighted mean of the dimensions below.
methodology.weightsLead: Weights are configurable in our admin and shown here so you can see what actually moves the number.
methodology.weightsFallback: Dimension weights are read from the risk model in our database and shown here when available.
methodology.evidenceBody: The score is only as good as the evidence behind it. Where you tell us you do not know something, we treat it as an open gap and score it accordingly. A supplier can lower its score by producing documents, not by arguing with the model.
methodology.limitationsLead: What this score does not tell you.
limitations: It is not a financial credit assessment. We do not review financial statements unless you ask us to.
It does not confirm that equipment exists or that a quality system runs day to day. That needs a site visit or an audit.
It is a point-in-time assessment. A score is valid as of the date it was produced.
It cannot detect a supplier that deliberately provides false documents, although document cross-checks reduce the gap.
Weights are our judgement, not an industry standard. We publish them so you can disagree with us in specific terms.
methodology.updateBody: We review weights when we make a material change to the model, and we record the version in use when a score is produced. Methodology changes are listed here with their date.
methodology.aiTitle: Where AI is used, and where it is not
methodology.aiBody: Scores come from the rules engine alone. A language model may summarize or explain a result in plain language, and it may draft the recommended actions. It does not decide the score, and it cannot see the weights as a variable it can adjust.

nodes.name: Pre-Production Inspection
nodes.when: Before production starts, on raw materials and the first sample.
nodes.what: Raw materials, equipment readiness, production plan, BOM, packaging materials, colours, dimensions, labels, samples, process requirements.
nodes.why: Catches the wrong thing before it is mass-produced. The cheapest defect is the one that never gets made.

nodes.name: During Production Inspection
nodes.when: While production is running, typically at 20–80% completion.
nodes.what: Product quality, dimensions, appearance, workmanship, function, quantity, defect rate, production progress, packaging, labels.
nodes.why: Problems found mid-run can still be fixed in time. Waiting for final inspection risks a whole batch you cannot repair.

nodes.name: Pre-Shipment Inspection
nodes.when: After production, before the goods leave the factory.
nodes.what: Quantity, appearance, dimensions, function, packaging, labels, barcodes, carton contents, specification, AQL sampling, defect classification, photos.
nodes.why: The final quality gate before balance payment. Most buyers start with PSI because it is the moment money is about to move.

nodes.name: Container Loading Supervision
nodes.when: During container loading at the factory or warehouse.
nodes.what: Container condition, container number, seal, product quantity, carton count, SKU, packaging, labels, loading process, mixed or wrong goods, short loading, photos, video.
nodes.why: Confirms that what you inspected is what actually gets loaded. Guards against substitution, short loading and mixed shipments.

faq.q: What is the difference between DUPRO and PSI?
faq.a: DUPRO (during production) is done while the goods are being made, usually at 20–80% completion, so problems can be fixed before the batch finishes. PSI (pre-shipment) is done after production, before the goods leave the factory, and is the final quality gate before balance payment. Many buyers do DUPRO for first orders and PSI for repeat orders; some do both.

faq.q: Do you have inspectors in every city?
faq.a: We do not publish a map of hundreds of inspectors because that would be a claim we cannot back. We match each order to a qualified independent inspector for the specific location and product category, and we confirm availability before quoting. If we cannot find the right person, we tell you instead of sending someone unsuitable.

faq.q: How much does an inspection cost?
faq.a: It depends on inspection type, scope, location, duration and the product. A standard single-site PSI in a major manufacturing hub is typically in the range of USD 200–350 per man-day, plus travel outside hub cities. Send us the factory location and we will quote it precisely.

faq.q: Can you inspect against my own checklist?
faq.a: Yes. If you have a buyer checklist or a spec sheet, send it with the request and the inspector will work to it. If you do not, we use a standard AQL-based inspection plan and tell you what we covered.

faq.q: How soon can an inspection be scheduled?
faq.a: In major hubs (Shenzhen, Dongguan, Guangzhou, Ningbo, Ho Chi Minh, Bangkok, Penang) we can usually schedule within 2–3 business days. Other locations need more lead time because the right inspector has to travel.

monitoring.honestNote: Monitoring lowers the chance of being surprised by a change that public records already show. It does not predict how a supplier will perform, and it cannot see a change that has not been recorded anywhere.
monitoring.recheckLead: Only items that leave a public or documentary trace. We do not re-check anything we cannot source.
recheckItems: Business registration status: active, revoked, relocated or renamed
Legal entity name and registered address
Certificate and audit report validity against the issuing scheme's database

Public records and adverse reports we can source and cite
The supplier's own declarations, compared against what we hold

cadenceItems.name: Quarterly
cadenceItems.note: For suppliers carrying your largest volume or your tightest compliance requirement.

cadenceItems.name: Twice a year
cadenceItems.note: The usual starting point for an active supplier.

cadenceItems.name: Once a year
cadenceItems.note: For suppliers you buy from occasionally, or to keep a dormant record current.

monitoring.alertLead: An alert goes out when a re-check returns something different from what we hold:
alertItems: Legal name or registered address changes
A certificate or audit report on file expires or is withdrawn
A new public record or adverse report we can cite
A scheduled re-check finds no change, and you still get a dated confirmation
monitoring.deliverLead: Every re-check produces a dated record, whether or not anything changed.
deliverItems: A dated re-check record for each supplier
An alert naming the fact that changed and the source that confirmed it
An updated report reflecting the current state of the record
The same evidence labels as a one-off check: reviewed, provided, restricted
monitoring.notCoveredLead: Monitoring inherits the limits of a verification. It does not extend them.
monitoring.pricingLead: Priced as a subscription, quoted per supplier per year, based on cadence and how many suppliers you want covered.
monitoring.pricingNote: No online checkout. Tell us the suppliers and the cadence, and we will quote.

faq.q: Is monitoring the same as a factory audit?
faq.a: No. An audit is an on-site assessment against a standard. Monitoring re-checks facts that leave a documentary or public trace. They answer different questions, and most buyers want both at different points.

faq.q: What if a supplier changes something between re-checks?
faq.a: Then the next re-check catches it, and the alert is dated to the day we confirmed it. A scheduled check cannot be continuous, and we do not claim it is.

faq.q: Can I add suppliers later?
faq.a: Yes. The subscription is quoted per supplier, so adding one means adjusting the quote rather than starting over.

faq.q: Do you visit the factory as part of monitoring?
faq.a: Not by default. Standard monitoring is a desk re-check of registers and documents. An on-site visit can be added at the cadence you choose and is quoted separately.

faq.q: Can a supplier pay to be monitored?
faq.a: No. Monitoring is bought by the buyer. A supplier cannot pay to change what a re-check reports.
